title: Expression, variable reference or runner mask where a workflow command would carry a token
summary: Workflow command lines and log text where the credential position holds an expression (${{ secrets.NAME }}), a shell variable reference ($NAME) as the add-mask argument or an environment-file value, a secret that expands to an empty string, or the runner's *** mask.
rationale: These are the same command shapes as the literal Case, so the command name and the NAME= prefix are the whole signal. The documentation says an expression is evaluated and substituted by the runner before the shell script runs, a variable reference is resolved by the shell at run time, an unset secret evaluates to an empty string, and a masked value is shown as ***. In each, the file or log text holds no token byte. A twin of the literal Case: only the secret position differs.

expectation.rationale: Not flagged. The text holds an expression, a variable reference, an empty value or the documented *** rendering of a masked value; no secret byte is present in it.

sources.supports: Before the shell script is run, the expressions inside ${{ }} are evaluated and then substituted with the resulting values.
Example masking an environment variable: run: echo "::add-mask::$MY_NAME"; when the value is printed in the log, you'll see *** instead of the value.
sources.locator: section: Masking a value in a log

sources.supports: If a secret has not been set, the return value of an expression referencing the secret (such as ${{ secrets.SuperSecret }}) will be an empty string.
sources.locator: section: Using secrets in a workflow

sources.supports: Example contents of the secrets context show each secret value as "***".

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04, before any scanner was consulted. Origin of the inputs: the command shapes are taken from the cited documentation examples (observed); the token is a synthetic value built from an existing authored base; the arrangement of one value in each command shape is evidence-derived, not an observed workflow. No workflow was executed and no value was tested. Whether a consumer reads a workflow file, an environment file or a runner log, and how it treats a mask, is the consumer's measurement contract and is not assumed here. The log lines in the fixtures are derived from the documentation's own example output (a masked value is printed as ***); they are not captured runner logs. Not covered: a mask that exposes part of a value, which the existing masks-ending-in-a-real-character Case already holds, and structured-data secrets that the documentation says may not be redacted correctly (unresolved, see the research notes).
